title: Cantilever beam
summary: Build the classic fixed-free beam from nothing: one body, one material, one load, and the theory to check it against.

steps.title: Start a Model
steps.explain: Everything in FEM Lab is a Command, and every Command is appended to the Journal — that list is the Model. `model.new` starts an empty one, named whatever you like.

steps.title: Choose display units
steps.explain: `model.setUnits` only changes how numbers are shown — millimetres and kilonewtons read naturally for a small steel part. The engine always works in SI underneath.

steps.title: Add the beam
steps.explain: `geometry.addBox` makes a Body from a size and an optional corner. A 1 m beam with a 100×100 mm square section is the shape every beam-theory textbook starts with. Its six faces are auto-named `beam.xmin` … `beam.zmax`.

steps.title: Define the material
steps.explain: `material.add` needs Young's modulus `E` and Poisson's ratio `nu`; `rho` (density) is only needed for gravity or modal analysis, but it costs nothing to record it now. `source` is where the numbers came from — useful in a report six months from now.

steps.title: Assign it to the beam
steps.explain: A Material exists independently of any Body until `material.assign` links them — the same Material can cover several Bodies at once.

steps.title: Mesh it
steps.explain: `mesh.set` chooses the Mesher and the element order. The lattice Mesher covers every Body with a structured grid — exact for a box like this one. `order: 1` gives linear (hex8) elements; a 25 mm size puts four elements across the 100 mm section.

steps.title: Fix the root
steps.explain: `constraint.fix` fixes displacement to zero on a Set — here, every node on the `beam.xmin` face, the definition of "cantilever" (clamped at one end, free at the other).

steps.title: Load the tip
steps.explain: `load.traction` spreads a total force over a face's area. A downward 1 kN at the free end (`beam.xmax`) is the loading beam theory calls `P` at the tip.

steps.title: Add a Step
steps.explain: A Step says which Constraints and Loads are active together and under which procedure — `static` is the only one so far. Nothing solves until you press Solve, but the Model is now complete and well posed.

steps.title: Check it against beam theory
steps.explain: Before you trust a solver, know what answer to expect. This is a textbook cantilever, so the closed form gives the tip deflection directly — compare it with the Result once you press Solve.
steps.theory:
Euler–Bernoulli beam theory: $\delta = \dfrac{P L^3}{3 E I}$, with $I = \dfrac{b h^3}{12}$ for a rectangular section.
$L = 1\,\mathrm{m}$, $P = 1\,\mathrm{kN}$, $E = 210\,\mathrm{GPa}$, $b = h = 100\,\mathrm{mm}$, so $I = 8.333\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^4}$.
$$\delta = \frac{1000 \times 1^3}{3 \times 2.1\times10^{11} \times 8.333\times10^{-6}} = 1.905\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m} = 0.1905\,\mathrm{mm}$$
The solved Model gives $0.1901\,\mathrm{mm}$ — $0.2\,\%$ below, which is what a hex8 mesh with incompatible modes and four elements through the depth should give. The formula itself ignores shear deflection, so it is not the exact answer either; for a beam this slender ($L/h = 10$) that is worth about $0.3\,\%$.
